CHAPTER 6: The Root Causes of Failed Pro.point: 瀑布式流程最大的问题是风险都堆在最后，用户验证太晚
CHAPTER 6: The Root Causes of Failed Pro.core: The biggest flaw of the old waterfall process has always been, and remains, that all the risk is at the end, which means that customer validation happens way too late.
CHAPTER 6: The Root Causes of Failed Pro.case: There are many reasons for an idea to not work out. The most common is that customers just aren't as excited about this idea as we are. So, they choose not to use it. Sometimes they want to use it and they try it out, but the product is so complicated that it's simply more trouble than it's worth, so users again choose not to use it. Sometimes the issue is that customers would love it, but it turns out to be much more involved to build than we thought, and we decide we simply can't afford the time and money required to deliver it.
CHAPTER 6: The Root Causes of Failed Pro.explain: 客户不够兴奋、产品太复杂用不起来、做起来比预想的贵，这三种失败原因在瀑布流程里都要等到开发上线后才会暴露。风险堆在末尾，前面投入的时间和钱就都白费了。

CHAPTER 8: Key Concepts.point: MVP 应该是原型而不是产品，否则学习成本过高
CHAPTER 8: Key Concepts.core: The MVP should be a prototype, not a product.
CHAPTER 8: Key Concepts.case: The vast majority of times I meet a team that has been working hard to create an MVP I am able to convince them that they could have achieved the same learning in a fraction of the time and effort. They have spent literally months building an MVP when they could have had this same learning in days or, sometimes, even in hours.
CHAPTER 8: Key Concepts.explain: 作者遇到的团队常花几个月做出产品级 MVP，而同样的学习用原型几天甚至几小时就能拿到。把 MVP 当产品来建，正是把本该便宜的实验做成了昂贵的交付。

CHAPTER 9: Principles of Strong Product.point: 产品团队要对自己那块产品的所有工作负完整责任
CHAPTER 9: Principles of Strong Product.core: One dimension of this is the type of work to be done, and it's important that a product team has responsibility for all the work—all the projects, features, bug fixes, performance work, optimizations, and content changes—everything and anything for their product.
CHAPTER 9: Principles of Strong Product.case: For example, you might be working on a team at eBay that's responsible for technology to detect and prevent fraud or tools and services for high‐volume sellers. Or, at Facebook, your team might be responsible for newsfeeds, an iOS native mobile app, or the capabilities required for a specific vertical market.
CHAPTER 9: Principles of Strong Product.explain: 在 eBay，一个团队可能专管反欺诈技术或大卖家工具；在 Facebook，可能专管信息流或 iOS 应用。每个团队拥有一块清晰的产品范围，功能、缺陷、性能都归它，才能长期积累专长和责任感。

CHAPTER 10: The Product Manager.point: 理解用户数据是产品经理不能外包的本职
CHAPTER 10: The Product Manager.core: You might have a data analyst to help you with this, but the analysis of the data and understanding you get of your customer is not something you can delegate.
CHAPTER 10: The Product Manager.caseTitle: 每天早上半小时看数据
CHAPTER 10: The Product Manager.case: A big part of knowing your customer is understanding what they're doing with your product. Most product managers start their day with half an hour or so in the analytics tools, understanding what's been happening in the past 24 hours. They're looking at sales analytics and usage analytics. They're looking at the results of A/B tests.
CHAPTER 10: The Product Manager.explain: 多数产品经理每天先花半小时看过去 24 小时的销售、使用数据和 A/B 测试结果。这种日常习惯说明，理解数据背后的用户行为必须亲自做，不能只等分析师交报告。

CHAPTER 23: The Alternative to Roadmaps.point: 给团队业务目标和衡量方式，让团队自己找解法
CHAPTER 23: The Alternative to Roadmaps.core: The idea behind business objectives is simple enough: tell the team what you need them to accomplish and how the results will be measured, and let the team figure out the best way to solve the problems.
CHAPTER 23: The Alternative to Roadmaps.caseTitle: 开通时间从 30 天到 3 小时
CHAPTER 23: The Alternative to Roadmaps.case: Consider this example of a business objective and a measurable, key result. Suppose your product currently requires 30 days for a new customer to onboard. But in order to scale effectively, management believes this needs to be reduced to three hours or less. That's a good example of a business objective for one or more product teams: “Dramatically reduce the time it takes for a new customer to go live.” And one of the measurable key results would be “Average new customer onboarding time less than three hours.”
CHAPTER 23: The Alternative to Roadmaps.explain: 管理层不指定做哪些功能，只给出大幅缩短新客户上线时间的目标，以及平均开通少于三小时的关键结果。团队怎么做由自己决定，但必须推动这个数字才算完成。

CHAPTER 24: Product Vision and Product S.point: 产品策略最好围绕一连串产品与市场匹配来排序
CHAPTER 24: Product Vision and Product S.core: For most types of businesses, I encourage teams to construct product strategy around a series of product/market fits.
CHAPTER 24: Product Vision and Product S.case: For consumer‐focused companies, we often structure each product/market fit around a different customer or user persona. For example, an education‐related service might have a strategy that targets high school students first, college students next, and then those already working but who want to learn new skills.
CHAPTER 24: Product Vision and Product S.explain: 一个教育服务先瞄准高中生，再做大学生，最后是想学新技能的在职人士。每一步只对一个人群追求产品与市场匹配，其他人群的点子先放着，这就是按顺序推进的产品策略。

CHAPTER 33: Principles of Product Discov.point: 强团队每周能测试一二十个点子，因为发现阶段的迭代很便宜
CHAPTER 33: Principles of Product Discov.core: To set your expectations, teams competent in modern discovery techniques can generally test on the order of 10–20 iterations per week.
CHAPTER 33: Principles of Product Discov.caseTitle: 止步于三人小组的迭代
CHAPTER 33: Principles of Product Discov.case: Also, realize that many iterations never make it beyond just you, your designer, and your tech lead. The very act of creating a prototype often exposes problems that cause you to change your mind. As a rule of thumb, an iteration in discovery should be at least an order of magnitude less time and effort than an iteration in delivery.
CHAPTER 33: Principles of Product Discov.explain: 很多点子只在产品经理、设计师和技术负责人之间就被原型暴露的问题否掉了。发现阶段一次迭代的成本比交付低一个数量级，所以每周试一二十个才可能。

CHAPTER 35: Opportunity Assessment Techn.point: 开工前就要想清楚怎样才算成功
CHAPTER 35: Opportunity Assessment Techn.core: We want to know at the outset what the measure of success is.
CHAPTER 35: Opportunity Assessment Techn.case: For example, if we're trying to reduce churn, would a 1 percent improvement be considered excellent or would be it be considered a waste of time?
CHAPTER 35: Opportunity Assessment Techn.explain: 同样是降低流失率，改善 1% 可能是优秀，也可能是浪费时间。作者用这个例子说明，若不事先约定关键结果的门槛，事后就无法判断这项发现工作是否值得。

CHAPTER 39: Customer Discovery Program T.point: 在一个目标市场拿到六个参考客户，才算达到产品与市场匹配
CHAPTER 39: Customer Discovery Program T.core: If we can get to the point where we have six reference customers in a specific target market, we will typically declare product/market fit for that market.
CHAPTER 39: Customer Discovery Program T.caseTitle: 按行业和地域攒参考客户
CHAPTER 39: Customer Discovery Program T.case: In the earlier chapters on product vision and strategy, we talked about the product strategy of pursuing a product vision by tackling one vertical market after another. For example, first develop six references for the financial services industry, then six for the manufacturing industry, and so on. Or you can expand geographically in this same manner (for example, first develop six references for the United States, six for Germany, and then six for Brazil, and so on).
CHAPTER 39: Customer Discovery Program T.explain: 先为金融服务业攒六个参考客户，再为制造业攒六个；或先美国、再德国、再巴西。每个市场都以六个参考客户作为匹配的标志，销售也只去卖已经验证过的市场。

CHAPTER 45: Principles of Prototypes.point: 做原型会逼人把问题想得更深，提早暴露问题
CHAPTER 45: Principles of Prototypes.core: Realize that one of the key benefits of any form of prototype is to force you to think through a problem at a substantially deeper level than if we just talk about it or write something down.
CHAPTER 45: Principles of Prototypes.case: The primary purpose of a prototype is to tackle one or more product risks (value, usability, feasibility, or viability) in discovery; however, in many cases, the prototype goes on to provide a second benefit, which is to communicate to the engineers and the broader organization what needs to be built. This is often referred to as prototype as spec.
CHAPTER 45: Principles of Prototypes.explain: 原型先用来在发现阶段应对价值、可用性、可行性和商业风险，之后还能直接作为规格交给工程师。同一个原型既暴露问题又传达要做什么，比口头或文字说明深入得多。

CHAPTER 51: Testing Value.point: 客户必须觉得产品明显更好，才愿意承受迁移的痛苦
CHAPTER 51: Testing Value.core: The customer must perceive your product to be substantially better to motivate them to buy your product and then wade through the pain and obstacles of migrating from their old solution.
CHAPTER 51: Testing Value.case: So many companies and product teams think all they need to do is match the features (referred to as feature parity), and then they don't understand why their product doesn't sell, even at a lower price.
CHAPTER 51: Testing Value.explain: 很多团队以为把竞品的功能补齐就行，结果即使价格更低也卖不动。因为客户换掉旧方案有迁移成本，功能相同不足以构成理由，只有明显更好才能打动他们。

CHAPTER 52: Demand Testing Techniques.point: 需求测试能同时拿到需求证据和一批愿意深聊的用户
CHAPTER 52: Demand Testing Techniques.core: Hopefully, you can see that this is very easy to do, and you can quickly collect two very useful things: (1) some good evidence on demand and (2) a list of users who are very ready and willing to talk with you about this specific new capability.
CHAPTER 52: Demand Testing Techniques.case: The demand‐testing technique is called a fake door demand test. The idea is that we put the button or menu item into the user experience exactly where we believe it should be. But, when the user clicks that button, rather than taking the user to the new feature, it instead takes the user to a special page that explains that you are studying the possibility of adding this new feature, and you are seeking customers to talk to about this. The page also provides a way for the user to volunteer (by providing their e‐mail or phone number, for example).
CHAPTER 52: Demand Testing Techniques.explain: 在功能该出现的位置放一个按钮，点进去只是一页说明正在考虑这个功能，并请用户留下邮箱或电话。点击率就是需求证据，留下联系方式的人就是后续访谈的对象，两样一次到手。

CHAPTER 53: Qualitative Value Testing Te.point: 当面测试时人们通常出于礼貌不说真话
CHAPTER 53: Qualitative Value Testing Te.core: The main challenge in testing value when you're sitting face to face with actual users and customers is that people are generally nice—and not willing to tell you what they really think.
CHAPTER 53: Qualitative Value Testing Te.caseTitle: 索要旧产品的登录信息
CHAPTER 53: Qualitative Value Testing Te.case: You can also ask people to provide the login credentials for whatever product they would be switching from (because you tell them there's a migration utility or something). Again, we don't really want their login and password—we just want to know if they value our product highly enough that they're truly willing to switch right then and there.
CHAPTER 53: Qualitative Value Testing Te.explain: 假称有迁移工具，请用户当场交出旧系统的账号。团队并不真要密码，只看对方是否愿意马上切换。用这种真实付出代替口头称赞，就能绕开出于礼貌的好评。

CHAPTER 54: Quantitative Value Testing T.point: 数据告诉你发生了什么，却解释不了为什么
CHAPTER 54: Quantitative Value Testing T.core: However, as powerful as the role of data is for us, the most important thing to keep in mind about analytics is that the data will shine a light on what is happening, but it won't explain why.
CHAPTER 54: Quantitative Value Testing T.case: I can't tell you how often we think we have something they'll love, and then we make it available to a limited group like this and we find that they are just not feeling it. Unfortunately, with a quantitative test like this all we know for sure is that they're not using it—we can't know why. That's when we'll follow up with a qualitative test to try and quickly learn why they're not as into it as we had hoped.
CHAPTER 54: Quantitative Value Testing T.explain: 团队以为用户会喜欢的功能，在邀请制测试中却没人用。定量数据只能确认没人用，原因要靠后续的定性测试去问。这说明定量和定性必须搭配使用。

CHAPTER 56: Testing Business Viability.point: 成功的产品要围绕销售渠道的长处和局限来设计
CHAPTER 56: Testing Business Viability.core: Successful products typically need to be designed around the strengths and limitations of the sales channel.
CHAPTER 56: Testing Business Viability.case: For example, a direct sales channel is very expensive, and this requires a high‐value product and price point. Or, you may have built up a sales channel with a certain set of skills, and if your new product requires a very different set of skills and knowledge, your sales force may completely reject the product.
CHAPTER 56: Testing Business Viability.explain: 直销成本高，要求产品高价值、高价位；如果新产品需要销售团队完全不同的技能，他们可能整体拒绝去卖。用户再喜欢、工程再能做，渠道不匹配产品也发不出去。

CHAPTER 64: Good Product Team/Bad Produc.point: 好团队与坏团队的差别不在细节，而在整套工作方式
CHAPTER 64: Good Product Team/Bad Produc.core: What I've learned is that there is a profound difference between how the very best product companies create technology products and all the rest.
CHAPTER 64: Good Product Team/Bad Produc.case: Good teams ensure that their engineers have time to try out the prototypes in discovery every day so that they can contribute their thoughts on how to make the product better. Bad teams show the prototypes to the engineers during sprint planning so they can estimate.
CHAPTER 64: Good Product Team/Bad Produc.explain: 好团队让工程师每天都在发现阶段试原型、提改进；坏团队直到冲刺计划才给工程师看，只为让他们估时。同一个原型，工程师是参与设计还是只负责估算，正体现两种工作方式的差别。
